label: Delimiter / first copy step of long sequences, gated by first token
explanation: Fires almost only in a narrow window around the phase switch: the last original token, the <DEL> step, and the first copy step (recall_idx 0-1 hold ~88% of mass; absolute t 8-10). It needs long sequences (L=9 holds 74% of mass, L=8 21%, never L<=5). Within that window, the first original token sets the firing rate: high for m, u, 1, j (precision 0.45-0.71 at step L+1), moderate for n, v, q, b, a, c, g, 0, and close to zero for d, k, o, t, r, s, f. The largest activations are at the first copy step (outputting orig(1), input = orig(0)) when orig(0) is m, u, or b. It does not fire in the early original phase or after recall_idx 2. The window alone (t 8-10, recall_idx<=1) covers 96% of mass but has precision 0.12. Adding the first-token set raises F1 only to ~0.39, so a good part of what drives it is unexplained (possibly other tokens in the prefix).
